$comment: QA scenario suite SOURCE — parametrized test cases for the full NLP contract (intent + taskType + entities). Expanded by buildQaScenarios.ts into v6/training_pipeline/benchmarks/qa_scenarios.jsonl. RULES: (1) These cases must NEVER enter training data — validate.ts leakage check enforces this. (2) status_today records the verified 2026-07-18 state so progress is measurable per release: PASS_EXPECTED | PARTIAL | FAIL_D1_NO_PERIOD_ROLES | FAIL_D2_DECODER_COLLAPSE | FAIL_D3_RESOLVER_GAP | FAIL_D4_SILENT_DEFAULT | FAIL_UNTRAINED_PATTERN | FAIL_UNMODELED. (3) Roles (period1/period2) and normalized values follow src/knowledge/entities/period.grammar.json.

classes.name: intent_boundary
classes.description: THE CRITICAL CLASS. Minimal pairs against LOAN_ANALYSIS (state of one loan NOW) and ADD_LIABILITY (recording a new loan). Same nouns, different intent — this is where the model will actually fail.

cases.notes: PAIR-A / DEBT side: trajectory. Nearly identical wording.

cases.notes: PAIR-B / LOAN side: a stored attribute.

classes.name: commitment_semantics
classes.description: Questions generated by OUR OWN product rules (BR_locks, BR_amount_forward, BR_today_paid, close/reopen). No generic LLM would invent these, but users hit them constantly because the product behaves this way.

cases.utterance: did this month's EMI already go out
cases.notes: BR_today_paid: a payment dated today is already history.

cases.utterance: my EMI went up what does that do to my payoff date
cases.notes: BR_amount_forward: new amount applies to upcoming cycles only.

cases.utterance: if I close this loan early what happens to my plan
cases.notes: BR_close_lifecycle: close preserves history, stamps endDate.

cases.utterance: which of my commitments are actually loans
cases.notes: Debt is a VIEW over commitments (category LOAN|CREDIT_CARD) — users don't know that boundary.

cases.utterance: what EMIs do I have coming up next month
cases.notes: Upcoming bucket. Borderline with a commitments listing — worth watching.

classes.name: incomplete_data
classes.description: The engine WITHHOLDS interest projections when interestRate is missing (RATE_MISSING — never fabricated). The model must still classify these correctly so the app can ask for the missing input instead of failing.

cases.utterance: why can't you tell me my payoff date
cases.notes: Triggered after a withheld projection. Answer should name the missing rate.

cases.utterance: I don't know my interest rate can you still estimate
cases.notes: Must NOT fabricate a rate — engine contract.

cases.utterance: how accurate is this debt projection
cases.notes: Maps to hasEstimatedValues / estimatedReasons.

classes.name: debt_negatives
classes.description: Debt-flavoured traps. Loan vocabulary present, but the correct answer is NOT a debt-freedom plan — either another intent or a refusal.

cases.utterance: should I take a loan to invest in stocks
cases.notes: PolicyGuard territory — leveraged investing advice, must not be answered as debt planning.

cases.utterance: what is the best home loan interest rate in the market
cases.notes: Product shopping — we have no market data. Must not be answered from the user's own loans.

cases.utterance: how do EMIs work
cases.notes: Education, not personal analysis. FinanceRouter's education regex owns it.
